title: The Calling of Apostles and the Nature of Psalmody
english: Seeing [them] through the 'Second' to draw them near, and through the 'Behold' to dazzle them with the truth, he prepares [them]. 481 Ps 45,9 The apostles also filled the inhabited world, running everywhere and recounting what had happened through him and performing wonders in his name. The Word is able also to call the nations to know the Creator of this [world] from the wonders seen concerning creation. 482 Ps 45,10 Having come and having destroyed the devil, the holder of the power of death, and the other evil powers, he has abolished wars even to the ends of the earth, that is, those passing from the lands; smashing the bow, the burning arrows of the evil one which were being shot, but also consuming with fire the door of unbelief opposite the door of faith. 483 Ps 45,11a No one sinning and being occupied with wandering is able to know God; for everyone sinning has not seen him, nor has he known him. He who desires to know God, having renounced every occupation, will know who God is, as the present saying says: 'Be at leisure and know.' This, therefore, the tyrant of Egypt, having perceived, subjects the Hebrews to occupations so that they may not attend to God, saying, 'Be at leisure' [as in, 'you are mere laborers']: for this reason they say, 'Let us go forth and serve our God.' 484 Ps 46,2a Since hands are often said to be instead of deeds, and the nations perform various things according to diverse customs before the visitation, the Savior, having visited men, commands a tumult to occur, that is, a harmony of the practical powers of the nations, tropically called hands. 485 Ps 46,2bβ Not only is a harmony of deeds sufficient for salvation, but also a right mind with these things. Therefore, he commands the nations to shout aloud in a voice of rejoicing along with the tumult. 486 Ps 46,3a And he is fearsome and worthy of reverence to those who hold piety toward him. 487 Ps 46,3b It is not doubtful that he reigns over the super-celestial [beings]. Concerning those wavering about the earth, even if he holds even it, the preceding verse is spoken, and especially because those describing providence even unto the lunar sphere do not wish [to admit] those under the earth to be under providence. 488 Ps 46,4.5 He also perceives thus: he has subjected...

He ordained the holy apostles as rulers and teachers of all peoples, both the circumcised and the Gentiles, under their feet, having chosen for himself an inheritance not other than that of Israel; he himself chose the election of Jacob. And he says [of] the whole people of the Hebrews, Jacob. From this the impartiality of God is known, that he loved nothing other than the beauty of Jacob; for in every way the one fearing him and working righteousness is acceptable to him. A voice is made significant by the shout of falling enemies, in which he rejoices (Ps 46:6); and it rises above our understanding when it is found.

The loud voice and the piercing of the dogmas are called the voice of a trumpet; for in the manifest and in the Gospel, a trumpet is taken up, as in the saying, 'When you do alms, do not sound a trumpet before you' (Matt 6:2), which is, do not make it manifest. Sing not only sensually according to the shadow of the law, but also spiritually according to the Gospel (Ps 46:7). Perhaps it commands doing this unceasingly and continuously through doubling. And this same doubling of singing must be raised up to the King Christ; for he is indeed Creator, God, and indeed Providential, King. Therefore, it is necessary to sing unceasingly to the same God and King.

He who sings must also understand the things being brought forth in the song (Ps 46:8b). It is not necessary that the thing happen primarily concerning the rhythm and the tone of the voice, but concerning the understanding of the things being sung. For God spares those who do not sing thus, but only make a noise, saying, 'Turn away from me the noise of your songs, and I will not hear the sound of your instruments.' But he sings intelligently, the one practicing according to the divine teachings and understanding them.

The rulers of the peoples are the apostles or the leaders of the churches, gathered with God Abraham, so that they might bring in the peoples who benefit through him; for their God is the God of children having become of Abraham. But stand firm, if the rulers of the peoples can be angels, concerning whom it has been said, 'He set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the angels of God' (Ps 46:10a), who also are gathered with God Abraham, since through faith they were made children.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Transformation of Souls and the Shipwreck of Bodies
english: Regarding Abraham, the portions which are found are rulers (Ps 46:10). The mighty ones of the earth are men who have lived rightly, exalting themselves by thinking of the things above and seeking the things above. For they, having been greatly exalted, being suspended by divine knowledge and virtue, have become of God; for the mighty ones of the earth, having become the possession of God, were exalted.

The joy of all the earth is a deep-rooted and good-rooted thing (Ps 47:3); perhaps there is no other one of him who said, 'I am the true vine' (John 15:1). For he himself is the joy of all the earth, being also the provider of joy.

It does not seem that some, having moved from wherever, were heard to have suffered, to signify from the appointed word; for they say that the Savior was crucified on the northern sides of Zion, there being the place of the skull (Ps 47:3).

But we say, following many writings, that the north is not anything other than the devil, according to the 'Exert yourself, O North, and come' (Job 37:7). This side is wicked men, just as they say the retainers of a ruler are his side. The wicked men who serve the devil, having previously been his side, transformed so much in virtue that they did not merely plunder Zion, but became its mountain (Ps 47:3-4). Paul, then, being a traitor, being a side of the north, plundered the body of the church which is Zion as it was transforming. And since the woman is called the side of the man, and the souls that became spouses to the devil, being his side through fellowship with him, became the mountain of Zion through transformation, just as the city of the great King Christ was plundered. For this word intends this, saying Zion [is] the mountain, which was formerly the side of the north or of the great king, we understanding it again as a great king by excellence of power but not of size. And in this city there are certain heavy and great dwellings in which God is known and the care of the city is grasped. These dwellings are of the same kind as the house which he builds upon the rock, he who heard the words of Jesus and did them (Ps 47:5-8). In the city the kings have come and into it...

Having been gathered together, having become the same, prepared by the same mind and the same judgment; but the kings are not those ruling according to God, such as Abraham was to someone, although not perceptibly ruling: 'You are a king from God in our midst' (Gen 26:2).

Not having seen the ancient ones who rose to such height from the north side, they marveled at the sight of Zion, being struck by the change occurring in the rational nature. And if one sees the bad becoming diligent and wise, marveling at the change, if he considers what might happen again—that those able to fall might be the diligent and wise—having thought this, he will cause trouble and shaking even to those who have greatly progressed in virtue, as if they were to seize the terror of dread.

Accompanying this is: 'The righteous groan in the places of the ungodly' (Ps 47:9), for when they fall, they become terrified. There are pains like those of a woman in childbirth. In the city of the great king, it is likely that souls have become pregnant from the bridegroom, and they have a time for delivery to form the offspring cast upon him, as if to labor to bring forth the mother's offspring.

The name of pains may signify those who are troubled and shaken, whom terror has seized. 'A mighty wind shall break the ships of Tarshish' (Job 41:31). The bodies are often called the ships of the souls in the Scripture, as also in 'Those going down into the sea in ships' (Ps 107:23). These bodies are not being crushed by the Divine Spirit striking them violently in essence, that is, being dissolved, so that at the time of the resurrection, incorruptible, strong, and promising spiritual things might come forth from corruptible, weak, and dishonorable, psychic kinds.

But these ships are not simply so, but are 'Tarshish,' changing the voice of Tarshish into the joy of discovery. For then the bodies, being crushed and dying, are praiseworthily broken, so that those nearby may discover the divine joy. While experiencing this in this life, we hear much concerning the heavenly city of God and the spiritual goods in it from prophetic words and other inspired Scripture. If, having been relocated...

title: The Instruction of the Power of Zion
english: Let us become from the earth in the upper Jerusalem, weighing together the things seen in it which we have heard of long ago, saying: Just as we heard, so also we shall see. For it is also the city of our God, since He Himself established it for eternity (Ps 47:9c-d). And the Savior is not spoken of in these things; for the Father shows Him, saying: I will build my city. He is the artisan and creator, while God is the one having the foundations of the city which all the righteous receive.

Just as your name is wonderful in all the land, so is your praise, since the earth is full of His praise (Ps 47:11ab). One must consider the ends and the borders of the earth, those who have passed from the earth into heaven, upon which the name of God and the praise have reached. Of the assembly named Zion, its Lord is the one whom those trusting in the Lord resemble (Ps 47:12a). 'Judah' is interpreted as confession, and the souls participating in the exercise of confession are the daughters of Judah. Perhaps also all the God-breathed Scripture is homonymous with the place in which Judah is given, in which God is known. The daughters, not of the Judah being given on either side, but approaching as much as possible the judgments of the Lord, are true and justified, and they will rejoice in the same way. And since the judgments of the Lord are unsearchable, they do not rejoice at the present, but they will rejoice face to face, approaching the truth then.

Regarding the ecclesiastical opinion, being a scrutiny of the truth and for this reason called Zion, it is fitting to take it up with wisdom, so that having reflected upon the doctrines of the truth, we may describe them in a circle to their own intellect. And since the city of God is surrounded on every side by the approaching enemies, and has towers constructed from which the approaching enemies can be scouted. And since the enemies of the city are now warring, it is necessary also for those in its towers to give guidance. It also agrees: 'Upon your walls I have set guards by day and by night, who will never be silent until the end' (Ps 47:12bc/13-15).

Being islands of the Lord; in this way even Wisdom is proclaimed upon the battlements of walls. Set therefore your heart, that is to say your mind, having scientifically attending to the power of Zion (this is the ecclesiastical teaching), and divide out analytically to each one attending to it.

For just as it is logical to divide things into essence and what has become, and genera into being, so also to divide the power of Zion into its weighty parts as much as possible; and its weighty parts are the individual contemplations in which the doctrines of piety dwell. Do this, so that you may narrate to another generation what our God himself is.

Since the former generation, having received the city and its power, was reproved as evil, adulterous, crooked, and perverted by its own heresy, having attended to the power of the city and dividing its weighty matters, you shall know the things concerning the calling of the Gentiles, which is another generation besides the former, in which you shall also narrate that this is not the God who, having done the aforementioned paradoxical things, cast away the former generation and called another and others. But this God, concerning whom the proposed theology is always the same and likewise has, unto the age and unto the age of ages; and He himself will shepherd us unto the ages according to what has been said: 'And the Lord shall shepherd his flock in strength' (Ps 48:2a).

Prepare your hearing, not the common one toward other animals, but the one of the inner man through which we comprehend what is heard, as the Savior says: 'He who has ears to hear, let him hear' (Ps 48:3a).

Since among the called Gentiles, some are dull of the matter and of the earthly mindset, but having been born sons of men, they rise up through knowledge and instruction, through lessons and examined words; and He calls not only the herd-like and grazing ones, but also the prudent, saying: 'Hear these, you who are born in the Gentiles and are sons of men.' For teachers are debtors not only to the wise but also to the foolish.
I bring forth wisdom from my mouth, having previously meditated understanding in my heart (Ps 48:4). For then one will be able to speak wisely.
